meta.note: Original CISSP-style practice questions. matching questions carry a prompts[] (left items numbered 1..n) and options[] (right items A..n); correct_answer encodes the pairing. sequence_ordering correct_answer lists option labels in correct order.

questions.subtopic: Canons of the Code of Ethics
questions.question: Two canons of the ISC2 Code of Ethics appear to conflict in a given situation. According to ISC2 guidance, how should the canons be applied to resolve the conflict?

options.label: A
options.text: Ignore the canons and defer entirely to local law

options.label: B
options.text: Apply whichever canon best protects the certified member from personal liability

options.label: C
options.text: Apply the canons in the order they are presented, giving earlier canons precedence over later ones

options.label: D
options.text: Apply the canon that most benefits the member's employer

explanation.why_correct: ISC2 states the canons are listed in order of precedence; when they conflict, the canon appearing first (protecting society and the public good) takes priority over later ones.

why_others_are_wrong.B: The Code exists to protect society and the profession, not to shield the member from liability.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Employer benefit is not the ordering principle; the public good comes first.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Law and the Code operate together; the Code is a condition of certification and is not discarded.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests whether the candidate knows the canons have a defined order of precedence, led by protecting society and the common good.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Code of Ethics

questions.subtopic: Canons of the Code of Ethics
questions.question: Which of the following is the FIRST canon of the ISC2 Code of Ethics?

options.label: A
options.text: Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly, and legally

options.label: C
options.text: Protect society, the common good, necessary public trust and confidence, and the infrastructure

options.label: D
options.text: Provide diligent and competent service to principals

explanation.why_correct: The first canon is to protect society, the common good, necessary public trust and confidence, and the infrastructure.

why_others_are_wrong.A: This is the second canon.
why_others_are_wrong.D: This is the third canon.
why_others_are_wrong.B: This is the fourth canon.

questions.exam_reasoning: Confirms recall of the ordered canons, with society/public good first.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Code of Ethics

questions.question: A CISSP discovers that a popular product their employer sells contains a serious, exploitable vulnerability that endangers many customers. Management instructs the CISSP to stay silent to protect quarterly sales. Applying the Code of Ethics, what should most strongly guide the CISSP's response?

options.label: A
options.text: The duty to provide service to principals means following the employer's instruction without question

options.label: B
options.text: The member should publicly disclose full exploit code to force a fix

options.label: C
options.text: The duty to protect society and the public good outweighs the employer's sales interest

options.label: D
options.text: The member should resign immediately and take no further action

explanation.why_correct: Protecting society and necessary public trust is the highest-precedence canon and outweighs short-term employer revenue; the member should pursue responsible remediation/disclosure.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Service to principals is a lower canon and never licenses endangering the public.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Resigning abandons the duty to protect society and does nothing to remediate the risk.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Releasing full exploit code recklessly harms customers and violates acting honorably and protecting society.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests precedence of public protection over employer pressure, and responsible rather than reckless action.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Code of Ethics

questions.question: Which TWO behaviors are consistent with the canon "Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly, and legally"? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Reporting findings truthfully even when they are unflattering to your employer

options.label: B
options.text: Exaggerating risk findings to win budget for a project you favor

options.label: C
options.text: Accurately representing your qualifications and the limits of your expertise

options.label: D
options.text: Withholding a conflict of interest from a client to keep an engagement

explanation.why_correct: Honest representation of qualifications and truthful reporting both embody honorable, honest, and just conduct.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Exaggerating findings is dishonest and manipulative, violating the canon.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Concealing a conflict of interest is dishonest and unjust.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes honest professional conduct from self-serving misrepresentation.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Code of Ethics

questions.question: According to ISC2, adherence to the Code of Ethics is best described as which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: A set of optional suggestions for new professionals

options.label: B
options.text: A condition of certification that all certified members must follow

options.label: C
options.text: A guideline that applies only while taking the exam

options.label: D
options.text: A legal statute enforced by government regulators

explanation.why_correct: ISC2 states that strict adherence to the Code is a condition of certification.

why_others_are_wrong.A: It is mandatory, not optional.
why_others_are_wrong.D: It is a professional code, not government law.
why_others_are_wrong.C: It applies throughout a member's certified career, not only during the exam.

questions.exam_reasoning: Confirms the Code is binding for the duration of certification.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Code of Ethics

questions.question: A CISSP is asked to take on consulting work that directly competes with a current client's interests. The most ethically appropriate first step is to:

options.label: A
options.text: Proceed but keep the two engagements secret from each other

options.label: B
options.text: Accept the work quietly because more income advances the profession

options.label: C
options.text: Disclose the potential conflict of interest to the affected parties

options.label: D
options.text: Decline all future consulting to avoid any appearance of conflict

explanation.why_correct: Acting honorably and justly requires disclosing conflicts of interest so affected parties can make informed decisions.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Income does not justify concealing a conflict; this violates honest/just conduct.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Blanket avoidance is unnecessary; disclosure and management of the conflict is the correct response.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Secrecy compounds the conflict and is dishonest.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests conflict-of-interest handling through transparency.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Code of Ethics

questions.question: Which action best fulfills the canon "Advance and protect the profession"?

options.label: A
options.text: Endorsing colleagues for skills you have not verified they possess

options.label: B
options.text: Refusing to share any knowledge so competitors cannot benefit

options.label: C
options.text: Publicly disparaging other certifications to elevate your own

options.label: D
options.text: Mentoring junior practitioners and discouraging unethical certification practices

explanation.why_correct: Mentoring and upholding ethical standards strengthens and protects the profession, fulfilling the fourth canon.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Hoarding knowledge does not advance the profession.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Endorsing unverified skills is dishonest and harms the profession's credibility.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Disparaging others is unprofessional and does not protect the profession.

questions.exam_reasoning: Links the fourth canon to constructive, honest professional behavior.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Code of Ethics

questions.question: Ensuring that data is not disclosed to unauthorized persons or processes is the definition of which security principle?

explanation.why_correct: Confidentiality ensures information is not disclosed to unauthorized parties—preventing people from seeing data they are not allowed to see.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Integrity concerns unauthorized alteration of data, not disclosure.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Availability concerns timely access for authorized users.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Non-repudiation prevents denial of an action's origin.

questions.exam_reasoning: Basic recall of the confidentiality definition.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Information Security Concepts

questions.question: An attacker modifies the dollar amounts stored in a bank's transaction database so that transfers are recorded incorrectly. Which element of the CIA triad is primarily violated?

explanation.why_correct: Unauthorized alteration of stored data is an integrity violation—preventing data from being changed by those not allowed to change it.

why_others_are_wrong.A: No unauthorized disclosure of data is described.
why_others_are_wrong.C: The data remains accessible; availability is not the primary concern.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Authenticity concerns the legitimacy of the source of an action, which is secondary here to the data alteration itself.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps an unauthorized-modification event to the integrity property.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Information Security Concepts

questions.question: A ransomware outbreak encrypts files on production servers, blocking authorized users from accessing them, though the data is never read or altered by the attacker beyond encryption. Which CIA property is most directly impacted?

explanation.why_correct: Blocking authorized access to data degrades availability—ensuring data is usable by authorized parties when needed.

why_others_are_wrong.B: The scenario specifies the data was not disclosed to unauthorized parties.
why_others_are_wrong.D: While encryption changes the bytes, the defining harm here is denial of access (availability), not silent corruption of legitimate content.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Non-repudiation is unrelated to access denial.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests recognizing availability as the property denied by ransomware encryption.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Information Security Concepts

questions.question: Which security property proves that data or an action originated from a particular subject who cannot later deny it, and is typically accomplished using cryptography?

explanation.why_correct: Non-repudiation proves the origin of data or actions so the originator cannot dispute it, commonly enforced with cryptographic digital signatures.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Availability concerns access, not proof of origin.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Confidentiality concerns disclosure, not proof of origin.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Redundancy is a reliability technique, not a CIA/authenticity property.

questions.exam_reasoning: Connects non-repudiation to cryptographic proof of origin.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Information Security Concepts

questions.question: A system verifies that a received message genuinely came from the claimed sender and was created by a legitimate source. Which property is being enforced?

explanation.why_correct: Authenticity ensures that data or an action came from a legitimate, verified source.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Availability concerns access, not source legitimacy.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Confidentiality concerns disclosure, not source legitimacy.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Anonymity is the opposite goal—hiding source identity.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes authenticity (legitimacy of source) from confidentiality and non-repudiation.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Information Security Concepts

questions.question: A hospital must keep patient monitoring systems running continuously, even if that means occasionally relaxing strict access prompts during emergencies. This design choice prioritizes which CIA property, and at the potential expense of which other?

options.label: A
options.text: Prioritizes non-repudiation, potentially at the expense of authenticity

options.label: B
options.text: Prioritizes availability, potentially at the expense of confidentiality

options.label: C
options.text: Prioritizes confidentiality, potentially at the expense of integrity

options.label: D
options.text: Prioritizes integrity, potentially at the expense of availability

explanation.why_correct: Keeping life-critical systems continuously usable favors availability; relaxing access prompts can weaken confidentiality controls.

why_others_are_wrong.C: The design relaxes access controls, which reduces confidentiality rather than prioritizing it.
why_others_are_wrong.D: No integrity trade-off is described; the trade is access continuity vs. access restriction.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Neither non-repudiation nor authenticity is the focus of continuous uptime decisions here.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests understanding that CIA properties can conflict and must be balanced to business/mission priorities.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Information Security Concepts

questions.question: Which TWO controls primarily support the integrity element of the CIA triad? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Cryptographic hashing of files to detect unauthorized changes

options.label: B
options.text: Redundant power supplies and failover clustering

options.label: C
options.text: Full-disk encryption of laptops at rest

options.label: D
options.text: Digital signatures that detect tampering with a message

explanation.why_correct: Hashing and digital signatures both detect unauthorized modification, directly supporting integrity.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Redundant power and failover support availability.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Full-disk encryption protects confidentiality of data at rest.

questions.exam_reasoning: Separates integrity-focused controls from availability- and confidentiality-focused ones.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Information Security Concepts

questions.question: Beyond confidentiality, integrity, and availability, which two additional properties does the study guide list as core information security concepts?

explanation.why_correct: The guide lists authenticity and non-repudiation alongside the CIA triad as core principles.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Redundancy and scalability are reliability/architecture qualities, not core security principles here.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Anonymity and obscurity are not the listed core principles.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Profitability and efficiency are business goals, not security properties.

questions.exam_reasoning: Confirms the expanded set of core properties taught in the guide.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Information Security Concepts

questions.question: A digital signature on an email both proves the message came from the sender and prevents the sender from later denying they sent it. The "cannot later deny" aspect specifically provides:

explanation.why_correct: The inability of the originator to deny the action is non-repudiation; the proof-of-source aspect is authenticity, and both are delivered by the signature.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Signatures do not, by themselves, hide message contents (confidentiality).
why_others_are_wrong.D: Availability is unrelated to signing.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Least privilege is an access principle, not a property of a signature.

questions.exam_reasoning: Forces a precise distinction between the authenticity and non-repudiation aspects of a signature.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Information Security Concepts

questions.question: Why does effective security governance require a top-down approach?

options.label: A
options.text: Only the most junior employees understand day-to-day security needs

options.label: B
options.text: Technical staff should define organizational risk appetite without executive input

options.label: C
options.text: Support and direction for security must originate with senior management and flow down to all personnel

options.label: D
options.text: Security controls should be selected by end users based on personal preference

explanation.why_correct: In a top-down approach, senior management sets direction and support, which then flows to middle management and all other personnel—essential for security to be effective.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Risk appetite is set by senior leadership, not technical staff alone.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Control selection is governed by policy and risk decisions, not user preference.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Governance authority and accountability rest with leadership, not solely junior staff.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the governance principle that security is driven and sponsored from the top.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Aligning Security and the Organization

questions.question: A long-term plan that outlines an organization's security goals and objectives over roughly a five-year horizon and is updated annually is best described as a:

explanation.why_correct: The strategic plan is the long-term plan outlining goals over a multi-year horizon and is typically reviewed/updated annually.

why_others_are_wrong.D: A tactical plan is mid-term (about one year) and supports the strategic plan.
why_others_are_wrong.B: An operational plan is short-term and highly detailed.
why_others_are_wrong.C: A runbook is an operational procedure, not a planning horizon.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes strategic, tactical, and operational planning horizons.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Aligning Security and the Organization

questions.question: Which plan is mid-term (approximately one year), designed to meet the security objectives defined in the strategic plan?

explanation.why_correct: The tactical plan is mid-term (about one year) and is designed to achieve the objectives set in the strategic plan.

why_others_are_wrong.A: The strategic plan is the long-term plan it supports.
why_others_are_wrong.B: The operational plan is short-term and more granular.
why_others_are_wrong.C: A capital plan is a financial/budget plan, not a security planning horizon.

questions.exam_reasoning: Confirms the tactical layer's horizon and purpose.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Aligning Security and the Organization

questions.question: The primary purpose of aligning the security program with organizational goals, culture, and operations is to:

options.label: A
options.text: Ensure security supports the business objectives rather than obstructing them

options.label: B
options.text: Allow security to operate independently of business strategy

options.label: C
options.text: Maximize the number of security controls regardless of business need

options.label: D
options.text: Shift all risk decisions to the IT help desk

explanation.why_correct: Security must support the organization's objectives, principles, and strategies; alignment tailors security to business needs so it enables rather than blocks the mission.

why_others_are_wrong.C: More controls without business justification is not alignment and may impede operations.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Operating independently of strategy is the opposite of alignment.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Risk decisions belong to management with appropriate authority, not the help desk.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the business-enablement purpose of security alignment.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Aligning Security and the Organization

questions.question: A company is acquiring a smaller competitor. From a security governance perspective, what is the most important action regarding the existing security plans?

options.label: A
options.text: Adopt the acquired company's controls wholesale without assessment

options.label: B
options.text: Review and update the security plans to account for the acquisition before integration proceeds

options.label: C
options.text: Delegate the decision to end users of both organizations

options.label: D
options.text: Freeze all security changes until the next annual strategic review

explanation.why_correct: Security plans must be reviewed and updated upon purchases, acquisitions, sales, or divestitures, because organizational structure changes affect risk and policy applicability.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Waiting for an annual review leaves the merged risk unmanaged during a high-risk period.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Adopting controls without assessment ignores due diligence and may import unknown risk.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Governance decisions of this magnitude rest with management, not end users.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the requirement to re-evaluate governance artifacts when organizational structure changes.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Aligning Security and the Organization

questions.question: Security governance is best defined as the practice of:

options.label: A
options.text: Installing and patching all servers in the environment

options.label: B
options.text: Performing day-to-day monitoring of firewall logs

options.label: C
options.text: Ethically aligning business objectives with applicable laws, standards, and regulations

options.label: D
options.text: Writing the source code for security tools

explanation.why_correct: Governance defines how to ethically align business objectives to laws, standards, or regulations and sets how management acts in stakeholders' best interest.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Patching is an operational task, not governance.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Coding tools is an engineering activity, not governance.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Log monitoring is an operational function, not governance.

questions.exam_reasoning: Separates strategic governance from operational/technical work.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Aligning Security and the Organization

questions.question: A new CISO finds that the security team has detailed daily procedures but no documented multi-year direction tied to business goals. Which planning gap should the CISO address FIRST to enable coherent governance?

options.label: A
options.text: Replace the ticketing system used by analysts

options.label: B
options.text: Rewrite each server's operational hardening checklist

options.label: C
options.text: Schedule more frequent firewall rule reviews

options.label: D
options.text: Establish a strategic plan that links security to long-term business objectives

explanation.why_correct: Without a strategic plan, tactical and operational activities lack direction; the strategic layer must be established first so lower layers align to business objectives.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Operational checklists already exist; the gap is strategic direction.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Tooling changes do not resolve the absence of strategic alignment.
why_others_are_wrong.C: More frequent reviews are operational tuning, not the governance gap.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests prioritization of the strategic layer when it is the missing governance element.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Aligning Security and the Organization

questions.question: Order the security plans from the LONGEST time horizon to the SHORTEST. (Provide the option labels in order.)

explanation.why_correct: Strategic (long-term, multi-year) is broadest, tactical (about one year) supports it, and operational (short-term, detailed) is the most immediate.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the relative time horizons of the three planning layers.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Aligning Security and the Organization

questions.question: For a security program to be effective, it must above all be:

options.label: A
options.text: Supported and sponsored by senior management

options.label: D
options.text: Kept secret from most of the organization

explanation.why_correct: The guide stresses that security must be supported by senior management to be effective, consistent with the top-down approach.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Consultants can assist, but executive sponsorship is the essential factor.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Awareness across the organization is needed; secrecy undermines effectiveness.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Perimeter-only focus ignores defense in depth and business alignment.

questions.exam_reasoning: Reinforces executive sponsorship as the foundation of an effective program.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Aligning Security and the Organization

questions.question: Which executive is responsible for the vision and strategy of the organization's security program?

explanation.why_correct: The CISO is responsible for the vision and strategy of the organization's security program.

why_others_are_wrong.B: The CFO is responsible for organizational finances and assets.
why_others_are_wrong.D: The CEO is responsible for everything relating to the organization overall, not specifically the security program strategy.
why_others_are_wrong.C: A data custodian implements data protection, an operational role.

questions.exam_reasoning: Recall of CISO accountability for security strategy.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: How does the responsibility of the CIO differ from that of the CISO?

options.label: A
options.text: The CIO handles payroll while the CISO handles marketing

options.label: B
options.text: They are identical roles with different titles

options.label: C
options.text: The CIO owns the vision/strategy for information systems; the CISO owns the vision/strategy for the security program

options.label: D
options.text: The CIO owns the security program; the CISO owns physical facilities

explanation.why_correct: The CIO is responsible for the vision and strategy of the organization's information systems, while the CISO is responsible for the vision and strategy of its security program.

why_others_are_wrong.D: The CISO, not the CIO, owns the security program; facilities are not the CISO's defining role.
why_others_are_wrong.B: They are distinct roles with different mandates.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Neither role is defined by payroll or marketing.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes information-systems leadership from security-program leadership.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: Who is responsible for the classification and protection of a given set of data?

explanation.why_correct: The data owner is responsible for the classification and protection decisions for their data.

why_others_are_wrong.D: The custodian implements protection but does not set classification.
why_others_are_wrong.C: The administrator maintains the system, a privileged operational role.
why_others_are_wrong.B: The auditor verifies compliance, not classification ownership.

questions.exam_reasoning: Separates data ownership (decision/accountability) from custody (implementation).

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: A data owner classifies a dataset as "Confidential" and specifies it must be encrypted at rest. The team member who actually configures and maintains that encryption on the storage system is acting as the:

explanation.why_correct: Implementing and maintaining the protection the owner specifies (e.g., encryption) is the custodian's responsibility.

why_others_are_wrong.A: The owner sets classification and protection requirements but does not necessarily implement them.
why_others_are_wrong.B: The steward provides subject-matter expertise for specific data, not hands-on protection implementation.
why_others_are_wrong.C: The security manager develops and manages the broader security program.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the owner-vs-custodian distinction in an applied setting.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: Which role provides subject-matter expertise for specific data, such as ensuring it is used and interpreted correctly?

explanation.why_correct: The data steward provides subject-matter expertise for specific data.

why_others_are_wrong.A: The custodian implements protection, not subject-matter expertise.
why_others_are_wrong.C: The administrator maintains the system.
why_others_are_wrong.D: A user simply accesses the system.

questions.exam_reasoning: Recall of the steward's SME function.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: Which security role is primarily responsible for detecting, analyzing, and responding to security threats and attacks?

explanation.why_correct: The security analyst detects, analyzes, and responds to security threats and attacks.

why_others_are_wrong.B: The security engineer designs, tests, and implements security solutions.
why_others_are_wrong.D: The security manager develops and manages the security program and its personnel.
why_others_are_wrong.C: The data owner sets classification and protection for data.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes analyst (detect/respond) from engineer (design/build) and manager (program).

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: To preserve independence, the role responsible for auditing compliance with the security policy should NOT also be the person who:

options.label: B
options.text: Implements and maintains the information systems being audited

explanation.why_correct: The auditor verifies compliance and must remain independent from the administrator who implements/maintains the systems—separating these duties avoids a conflict of interest.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Reading awareness emails does not compromise audit independence.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Attending meetings is unrelated to audit independence.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Completing training does not conflict with the audit role.

questions.exam_reasoning: Connects auditor independence to separation of duties from system administration.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: In the system roles described by the guide, the administrator is best characterized as a:

options.label: A
options.text: Privileged role responsible for implementing and maintaining the information system

options.label: B
options.text: Non-privileged subject who only accesses the system

options.label: C
options.text: Role that sets the organization's risk appetite

options.label: D
options.text: External regulator who enforces national law

explanation.why_correct: The administrator is a privileged role responsible for implementing and maintaining the information system.

why_others_are_wrong.B: That describes a user, not an administrator.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Regulators are external to the system role model.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Risk appetite is set by senior management, not the administrator.

questions.exam_reasoning: Recall of the administrator as a privileged operational role.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: Boards and committees primarily exist within an organization to:

options.label: B
options.text: Make key organizational decisions and provide oversight

explanation.why_correct: Boards and committees are groups responsible for making key organizational decisions and providing governance oversight.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Patching is an operational task handled by IT staff.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Coding is an engineering function.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Help-desk response is an operational support task.

questions.exam_reasoning: Reinforces the governance/oversight purpose of boards and committees.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: After a major breach, regulators ask who holds ultimate accountability for everything relating to the organization, including its overall risk posture. The most accurate answer is the:

explanation.why_correct: The CEO is responsible for everything relating to the organization, holding ultimate accountability even when functions are delegated.

why_others_are_wrong.C: The analyst handles detection and response, not ultimate organizational accountability.
why_others_are_wrong.B: The custodian implements data protection at an operational level.
why_others_are_wrong.A: The technician provides support and has no organizational accountability.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests that ultimate accountability rests at the top even when duties are delegated.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is responsible for everything relating to:

explanation.why_correct: The CFO is responsible for everything relating to organizational finances and assets.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Security controls fall under the CISO.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Code repositories fall under engineering/IT, not the CFO.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Badge issuance is a physical security operational task.

questions.exam_reasoning: Recall of CFO scope.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: Which TWO statements correctly describe data-related responsibilities? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: The data custodian implements the protection mechanisms for the data

options.label: B
options.text: The data owner decides the classification level of the data

options.label: C
options.text: The auditor implements encryption on the storage array

options.label: D
options.text: The user defines the organization's data retention policy

explanation.why_correct: Owners set classification; custodians implement protection—the canonical separation between accountability and implementation.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Retention policy is set by owners/management, not end users.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Auditors verify compliance and must stay independent of implementation tasks like configuring encryption.

questions.exam_reasoning: Reinforces the owner/custodian/auditor/user separation.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: Match each role (1-4) to its primary responsibility (A-D).

options.label: A
options.text: Sets data classification and protection requirements

options.label: B
options.text: Implements and maintains data protection mechanisms

options.label: C
options.text: Verifies compliance with the security policy

options.label: D
options.text: Designs, tests, and implements security solutions

explanation.why_correct: Data Owner → sets classification/protection (B); Data Custodian → implements protection (A); Auditor → verifies compliance (D); Security Engineer → designs/tests/implements solutions (C).

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests precise mapping of governance and operational roles to their defining duties.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: In the system role model, a "user" is best defined as:

options.label: A
options.text: The independent reviewer of policy compliance

options.label: B
options.text: The person who sets the organization's strategic security vision

options.label: C
options.text: The privileged maintainer of the system

options.label: D
options.text: A subject with access to the information system

explanation.why_correct: A user is a subject with access to the information system.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Strategic vision is the CISO's responsibility.
why_others_are_wrong.C: The privileged maintainer is the administrator.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Independent compliance review is the auditor's role.

questions.exam_reasoning: Recall of the user definition within the system role model.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Organizational Roles and Responsibilities

questions.question: Security governance "sets the stage for how an organization's management will act." Acting in this capacity, management is expected to act primarily in the best interest of:

explanation.why_correct: Governance establishes that management acts in the best interest of the business stakeholders.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Individual technical skill does not define whose interests governance serves.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Acting for attackers is nonsensical and contrary to governance.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Cost minimization is not the governing interest; stakeholder interest is.

questions.exam_reasoning: Anchors governance to stakeholder interest as the guiding principle.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Aligning Security and the Organization

questions.question: In the awareness/training/education model, which activity is intended to CHANGE behavior by enhancing the specific skills employees need to follow security policies?

explanation.why_correct: Training focuses on enhancing skills so personnel can adhere to security policies, often via hands-on sessions and role-specific instruction.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Awareness reinforces what to pay attention to (the "what"), not deep skill-building.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Education provides comprehensive knowledge beyond immediate job functions.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Certification renewal is an administrative credential activity, not the behavior-changing skill layer.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes the purpose of training (skills) from awareness (attention) and education (broad knowledge).

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Security Awareness Training and Education

questions.question: Posters, emails, and periodic reminders about security protocols are common methods used to deliver which program element?

explanation.why_correct: Awareness uses methods such as emails, posters, workshops, and regular updates to keep security top-of-mind.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Education uses formal courses, certifications, and advanced programs.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Penetration testing is an assessment activity, not awareness delivery.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Disaster recovery is a continuity activity, not awareness delivery.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps common low-cost reminders to the awareness layer.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Security Awareness Training and Education

questions.question: A CISO wants to evaluate whether the security awareness program is actually reducing risk. Which approach best measures program effectiveness rather than mere completion?

options.label: A
options.text: Measure how many posters were printed and displayed

options.label: B
options.text: Count how many employees opened the awareness email

options.label: C
options.text: Track click rates on simulated phishing campaigns over time and correlate with reported incidents

options.label: D
options.text: Record the total budget spent on the program

explanation.why_correct: Evaluating effectiveness requires outcome metrics—e.g., changes in simulated-phishing susceptibility and incident trends—rather than activity counts.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Email opens measure exposure, not behavior change or risk reduction.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Poster counts are an activity input, not an effectiveness outcome.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Spend is a cost input and says nothing about effectiveness.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests evaluating awareness programs by behavioral outcomes, not vanity/activity metrics.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Security Awareness Training and Education

questions.question: Targeted training programs that ensure adherence to standards such as PCI DSS, FISMA, and ISO 27001 are an example of using awareness/training to achieve:

explanation.why_correct: Training can be designed to achieve regulatory compliance with standards like PCI DSS, FISMA, and ISO 27001.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Segmentation is a network control, not a training outcome.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Key escrow is a cryptographic process.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Perimeter defense is a physical control.

questions.exam_reasoning: Connects training programs to compliance objectives.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Practical Applications and Scenarios

questions.question: Security policies and procedures distributed to employees during onboarding and at regular intervals are an example of which control category?

explanation.why_correct: Policies and procedures delivered through onboarding and recurring training are administrative (managerial) controls.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Technical controls are implemented in hardware/software.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Physical controls protect tangible assets and facilities.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Compensating controls substitute for an infeasible primary control; that is not what is described here.

questions.exam_reasoning: Classifies policy/procedure distribution as administrative control.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Practical Applications and Scenarios

questions.question: Social engineering is best described as:

options.label: A
options.text: A method for encrypting data in transit

options.label: B
options.text: A process for classifying organizational assets

options.label: C
options.text: A technique for load-balancing network traffic

options.label: D
options.text: Psychological manipulation that deceives individuals into divulging confidential information

explanation.why_correct: Social engineering uses psychological manipulation to deceive people into divulging confidential or personal information, often for fraud.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Encryption protects data, not a manipulation technique.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Load balancing is a networking function.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Asset classification is a governance/asset-security activity.

questions.exam_reasoning: Confirms the human-manipulation nature of social engineering.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Social Engineering

questions.question: A finance employee receives a highly customized email that references their manager by name and a real internal project, attempting to trick them into wiring funds. This is best classified as:

explanation.why_correct: Spear phishing is a targeted phishing attack customized to a specific individual or group using personalized details.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Vishing is voice phishing conducted over the phone.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Smishing is phishing via SMS messages.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Dumpster diving is sifting through trash for information, a physical tactic.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes targeted (spear) phishing from channel-specific variants.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Social Engineering

questions.question: A phishing attack that specifically targets a high-value individual such as a CEO or CFO is known as:

explanation.why_correct: Whaling is phishing aimed at high-profile, high-value targets such as senior executives.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Smishing uses SMS as the delivery channel.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Spim is spam over instant messaging.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Tailgating is a physical access tactic.

questions.exam_reasoning: Identifies whaling as executive-targeted phishing.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Social Engineering

questions.question: Phishing conducted through SMS text messages is called:

explanation.why_correct: Smishing is phishing carried out through SMS messages.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Vishing is voice phishing over the phone.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Whaling targets high-value executives.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Pretexting uses a fabricated scenario to obtain information.

questions.exam_reasoning: Channel recall: SMS = smishing.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Social Engineering

questions.question: An attacker calls the help desk pretending to be a traveling executive locked out of their account, inventing a detailed but false back-story to pressure the agent into a password reset. This technique is:

explanation.why_correct: Pretexting uses a fabricated but believable scenario (a pretext) to manipulate a target into providing access or information.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Quid pro quo offers a benefit in exchange for information or access.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Shoulder surfing is visually observing someone to capture information.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Piggybacking is gaining physical entry by getting someone to hold a door.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests recognition of the fabricated-scenario hallmark of pretexting.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Social Engineering

questions.question: A caller posing as IT support offers to "fix a slow computer" in exchange for the employee's login credentials. Which technique does this represent?

explanation.why_correct: Quid pro quo offers something of value (help/fix) in exchange for information or access.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Whaling targets executives specifically.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Smishing uses SMS.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Dumpster diving searches trash for information.

questions.exam_reasoning: Identifies the "something for something" exchange as quid pro quo.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Social Engineering

questions.question: An unauthorized person follows an employee through a secured door WITHOUT the employee's knowledge. This is best described as:

explanation.why_correct: Tailgating is following someone through a secure door without their knowledge or consent.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Piggybacking involves the employee knowingly holding the door (often via an empathy ploy).
why_others_are_wrong.B: Shoulder surfing is observing to capture information such as passwords.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Vishing is voice phishing.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes tailgating (without knowledge) from piggybacking (with consent).

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Physical Social Engineering Tactics

questions.question: The KEY difference between piggybacking and tailgating, as taught in the guide, is that piggybacking:

options.label: A
options.text: Always requires cloning an access badge

options.label: B
options.text: Is a purely digital, network-based attack

options.label: C
options.text: Only occurs in fully unmanned facilities

options.label: D
options.text: Involves the authorized person knowingly granting entry, often after being asked to hold the door

explanation.why_correct: Piggybacking is gaining access by getting someone to hold the door—i.e., with the authorized person's knowledge/consent—whereas tailgating happens without their knowledge.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Badge cloning is a separate technique and not what defines piggybacking.
why_others_are_wrong.C: It typically occurs precisely where people are present to be manipulated.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Both are physical entry tactics, not network attacks.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the consent/knowledge distinction between the two physical tactics.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Physical Social Engineering Tactics

questions.question: A receptionist is unsure whether a visitor claiming to be a vendor is legitimate. Which TWO actions align with social-engineering defenses? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Grant access immediately to avoid appearing rude to the vendor

options.label: B
options.text: Require valid identification from the visitor before granting access

options.label: C
options.text: Ask the visitor to hold the door for the next person entering

options.label: D
options.text: Verify the visitor by contacting their associated company or team

explanation.why_correct: Defenses require valid identification for all personnel and visitors and verification of unknown individuals (e.g., by contacting their associated company or team) before granting access.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Politeness must not override verification; granting access immediately enables impersonation.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Encouraging door-holding facilitates piggybacking and defeats access control.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests identification and verification as the front-line defenses against in-person social engineering.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Defense Against Social Engineering

questions.question: Which control is the MOST effective broad defense against social engineering, given that it targets the human element?

options.label: A
options.text: Ongoing security awareness training that teaches staff to recognize and respond to manipulation

explanation.why_correct: Because social engineering exploits people, security awareness training that helps personnel recognize and respond to attempts is the primary defense.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Bandwidth has no bearing on human manipulation.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Blanket attachment blocking is impractical and does not address phone, in-person, or SMS vectors.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Office temperature is irrelevant to social engineering.

questions.exam_reasoning: Reinforces that the human-focused control (training) best counters human-focused attacks.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Defense Against Social Engineering

questions.question: Match each social-engineering technique (1-4) to its description (A-D).

options.label: A
options.text: Observing a person to capture information such as passwords

options.label: B
options.text: Phishing carried out through SMS messages

options.label: C
options.text: Voice phishing conducted over the phone

options.label: D
options.text: Sifting through discarded trash to find sensitive information

explanation.why_correct: Vishing → phone voice phishing (B); Smishing → SMS phishing (C); Shoulder surfing → visually observing to capture info (D); Dumpster diving → trash sifting (A).

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests precise mapping of social-engineering techniques to their channels/methods.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Social Engineering

questions.question: Which personnel control prevents any single individual from having excessive control over a critical business function?

explanation.why_correct: Separation of duties divides critical functions so no single person can complete a sensitive process alone, reducing fraud and error.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Least privilege limits access to the minimum needed, but does not by itself split a single function across people.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Need to know restricts information access, not control over a whole function.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Job rotation moves staff between roles; it is a related but distinct control.

questions.exam_reasoning: Separates SoD (split a function) from least privilege and need-to-know.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Key Security Controls for Personnel Management

questions.subtopic: Least privilege vs need to know
questions.question: An employee has the system rights to open a folder (their role allows it) but should not view a specific file inside it because it is unrelated to their current task. Restricting that specific file most directly enforces:

explanation.why_correct: Need to know restricts access to specific information to only those who require it for their duties, even when broader privileges technically permit access.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Least privilege limits the rights/permissions granted; here the rights exist but the specific information is still not needed.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Separation of duties divides a function among people; it is not about a single file's relevance.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Mandatory vacation is a fraud-detection control, not access scoping.

questions.exam_reasoning: Forces the subtle distinction between least privilege (rights) and need-to-know (specific information relevance).

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Key Security Controls for Personnel Management

questions.question: Ensuring personnel have only the minimum level of access required to perform their job functions defines:

explanation.why_correct: Least privilege grants the minimum access necessary to perform one's duties.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Separation of duties divides critical functions among multiple people.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Defense in depth layers multiple controls.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Due diligence is the ongoing effort to keep controls effective.

questions.exam_reasoning: Basic recall of the least-privilege definition.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Key Security Controls for Personnel Management

questions.question: Place the following personnel-security activities in the order they normally occur across the employment lifecycle. (Provide the option labels in order.)

options.label: A
options.text: Offboarding: access revocation and asset return

options.label: B
options.text: Ongoing access management under least privilege

options.label: D
options.text: Onboarding security training and policy acknowledgement

explanation.why_correct: The lifecycle runs from pre-hire screening, to onboarding, to ongoing management during employment, to offboarding at termination.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests understanding of the personnel-security lifecycle order.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Personnel Security Policies

questions.question: During hiring, screening and background checks primarily serve to:

options.label: A
options.text: Verify candidates' suitability and trustworthiness before granting access

options.label: B
options.text: Replace the need for onboarding training

options.label: C
options.text: Determine the company's annual marketing budget

options.label: D
options.text: Eliminate the need for least privilege after hire

explanation.why_correct: Screening and background checks (criminal history, prior employment, education, etc.) help ensure candidate suitability and trustworthiness.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Screening does not replace onboarding training.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Least privilege still applies after hire regardless of screening.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Budgeting is unrelated to personnel screening.

questions.exam_reasoning: Connects pre-employment screening to trust establishment.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Hiring Process

questions.question: Which agreement binds employees to protect sensitive information both during and after their employment?

explanation.why_correct: An NDA binds employees to protect sensitive information during and after their tenure.

why_others_are_wrong.A: A non-compete restricts joining competitors, not information protection per se.
why_others_are_wrong.D: An AUP defines acceptable use of company resources.
why_others_are_wrong.B: An SLA defines service expectations between parties, often with vendors.

questions.exam_reasoning: Recall of the NDA's confidentiality purpose spanning employment and beyond.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Employee Agreements and Policies

questions.question: A clause that prevents an employee from joining competing firms for a specified period after leaving is a:

explanation.why_correct: A non-compete agreement prevents employees from joining competing firms for a defined post-employment period.

why_others_are_wrong.A: An NDA protects confidential information, not employment with competitors.
why_others_are_wrong.B: An AUP governs use of company resources.
why_others_are_wrong.C: An MOU is a broad statement of intent between parties.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes non-compete from NDA and AUP.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Employee Agreements and Policies

questions.question: Which document defines the acceptable and secure ways employees may use company resources?

explanation.why_correct: The AUP defines acceptable and secure ways employees can use company resources.

why_others_are_wrong.C: An NDA covers confidentiality of information.
why_others_are_wrong.B: A non-compete restricts future competing employment.
why_others_are_wrong.D: A BIA assesses impacts for continuity planning.

questions.exam_reasoning: Recall of AUP purpose.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Employee Agreements and Policies

questions.question: During onboarding, new hires are granted access to company resources based on which principle?

explanation.why_correct: Onboarding grants access to company resources based on the principle of least privilege.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Convenience-driven over-provisioning increases risk.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Default all-access violates least privilege.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Anonymous access undermines accountability.

questions.exam_reasoning: Ties onboarding provisioning to least privilege.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Onboarding Process

questions.question: An employee is being terminated for cause. From a security standpoint, which action is MOST time-critical during offboarding?

options.label: B
options.text: Updating the company org chart graphics

options.label: D
options.text: Promptly revoking the employee's access rights to systems and facilities

explanation.why_correct: Offboarding must securely terminate access rights (and retrieve assets); prompt access revocation limits the window for retaliatory or unauthorized actions.

why_others_are_wrong.A: A terminated employee will not receive a future review; this is irrelevant.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Org-chart graphics are administrative and not security-critical.
why_others_are_wrong.C: A farewell announcement is not a security control.

questions.exam_reasoning: Prioritizes access revocation as the urgent offboarding security task.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Offboarding Process

questions.question: Exit interviews during offboarding primarily help the organization to:

options.label: A
options.text: Understand potential security concerns and reinforce confidentiality obligations

options.label: B
options.text: Assign the employee additional system privileges

options.label: C
options.text: Negotiate the departing employee's new salary

options.label: D
options.text: Skip the need for access revocation

explanation.why_correct: Exit interviews help surface potential security concerns and reinforce confidentiality agreements as the employee departs.

why_others_are_wrong.C: Salary negotiation is irrelevant to a departing employee's security exit.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Offboarding revokes, not expands, privileges.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Access revocation is still required; the interview does not replace it.

questions.exam_reasoning: Connects exit interviews to confidentiality reinforcement and concern identification.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Offboarding Process

questions.question: Requiring new hires to sign documents acknowledging they understand and will comply with security policies is called:

explanation.why_correct: Policy acknowledgement requires new hires to sign agreements confirming understanding of and compliance with security policies.

why_others_are_wrong.D: Risk acceptance is a risk-response decision by management.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Penetration testing is a security assessment.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Data classification is an asset-security activity.

questions.exam_reasoning: Recall of the policy-acknowledgement step.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Onboarding Process

questions.question: Which control allows an employee under threat to silently signal for help without alerting the aggressor?

options.label: C
options.text: A duress code or silent alarm

explanation.why_correct: Duress codes or silent alarms let personnel alert security discreetly without escalating a dangerous situation.

why_others_are_wrong.B: A loud page would alert the aggressor and escalate danger.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Public posts are slow, visible, and unreliable for emergencies.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Newsletters are not emergency signaling mechanisms.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the purpose of duress signaling—covert alerting.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Personnel Safety and Security

questions.question: To protect organizational resources accessed by traveling employees over untrusted networks, the guide recommends:

options.label: C
options.text: Using VPNs for secure remote access

explanation.why_correct: Travel security includes using VPNs for secure remote access to organizational resources.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Disabling authentication removes a critical control.
why_others_are_wrong.B: Emailing passwords exposes credentials.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Public itineraries increase personal and physical risk.

questions.exam_reasoning: Connects travel security to encrypted remote-access (VPN).

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Personnel Safety and Security

questions.question: During a building fire, an automated system can either keep electronic doors locked to protect a data center or unlock egress routes to let people exit. Which choice aligns with security best practice?

options.label: A
options.text: Lock only the exits nearest to executives

options.label: B
options.text: Keep all doors locked to protect the data center at all costs

options.label: C
options.text: Unlock egress routes—human life safety takes precedence over asset protection

options.label: D
options.text: Disable fire alarms to avoid panic

explanation.why_correct: Human safety is the highest priority; emergency systems should fail to a state that permits safe egress, even at some risk to assets.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Trapping people to protect equipment is never acceptable; life safety comes first.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Selective locking still endangers lives and is discriminatory and unsafe.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Disabling alarms removes life-saving warning and is dangerous.

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the overriding principle that life safety outranks asset protection.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Personnel Safety and Security

questions.question: A comprehensive personnel safety program should include emergency communication that:

options.label: A
options.text: Relies solely on word of mouth between employees

options.label: B
options.text: Is documented only in the CEO's personal notebook

options.label: C
options.text: Is tested once at company founding and never again

options.label: D
options.text: Provides clear protocols, emergency contacts, and procedures for reporting incidents

explanation.why_correct: Emergency communication requires clear protocols and a plan including emergency contact numbers and reporting procedures.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Word of mouth is unreliable in emergencies.
why_others_are_wrong.B: A single private copy is not accessible when needed.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Plans must be regularly tested and drilled, not set once and forgotten.

questions.exam_reasoning: Highlights structured, documented, testable emergency communication.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Management Concepts > Personnel Safety and Security

questions.question: Which statement BEST distinguishes due care from due diligence?

options.label: A
options.text: Due care is implementing reasonable security measures; due diligence is the ongoing effort to ensure they remain effective

options.label: B
options.text: Due care is a one-time audit; due diligence is ignoring known risks

options.label: C
options.text: They are interchangeable terms with no practical difference

options.label: D
options.text: Due care applies only to vendors; due diligence applies only to employees

explanation.why_correct: Due care is the responsibility to implement effective security measures; due diligence is the ongoing effort to keep those measures updated and effective.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Due diligence is continuous attention to risk, not ignoring it.
why_others_are_wrong.D: Both concepts apply broadly, not to a single population.
why_others_are_wrong.C: They are distinct: doing the right thing (care) vs. continually verifying it (diligence).

questions.exam_reasoning: Tests the canonical care-vs-diligence distinction.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Security Governance and Compliance > Due Care and Due Diligence

questions.question: An organization deployed strong controls two years ago but never revisited them; a breach exploited a control that had since become outdated. Which failure does this MOST clearly illustrate?

options.label: B
options.text: Lack of due care (never implementing any controls)

options.label: D
options.text: Lack of due diligence (ongoing review and updating)

explanation.why_correct: Controls were implemented (due care) but never maintained or reassessed—an absence of due diligence, the ongoing effort to keep controls effective.

why_others_are_wrong.B: Controls were implemented, so due care was at least initially exercised; the gap is in maintenance.
why_others_are_wrong.C: Least privilege did not cause the outdated-control failure.
why_others_are_wrong.A: Awareness training is unrelated to the unmaintained technical control.

questions.exam_reasoning: Maps a "set and forget" failure specifically to missing due diligence.

why_others_are_wrong.B: CFAA addresses computer fraud and abuse.

questions.question: Which statement about the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) is correct?

options.text: It is a US federal statute enforced by the Department of Justice

questions.question: Under GDPR, the party that determines the purposes and means of processing personal data is the:

why_others_are_wrong.D: The supervisory authority is the regulator, not the processing decision-maker.

questions.question: A customer asks a company to delete all personal data it holds about them. Which GDPR right are they exercising?

why_others_are_wrong.A: Restriction limits how data is used, not deletion.

why_others_are_wrong.A: Budget-setting is not a GDPR data-subject right.

questions.question: An inquiry initiated by a government regulator to determine whether an organization complied with a specific industry rule is a(n):

why_others_are_wrong.D: Civil investigations concern disputes between private parties.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes regulatory from administrative, criminal, and civil investigations.

source_reference.syllabus_section: Domain 1 > Incident Management > Investigations (administrative, criminal, civil, regulatory)

questions.question: Which security document provides detailed, step-by-step instructions on how to implement a standard?

explanation.why_correct: A procedure provides detailed, step-by-step instructions on how to implement standards.

why_others_are_wrong.D: A policy is a high-level statement of management intent and goals.
why_others_are_wrong.C: A baseline defines the minimum security controls required to meet a standard.
why_others_are_wrong.B: A guideline offers recommendations/best practices when standards are unclear or non-specific.

questions.exam_reasoning: Distinguishes procedure (how-to steps) from policy, baseline, and guideline.
